summary: A name search is blind to how a name stores a letter with an accent: as one character (`é`, what a keyboard types) or as the letter and then its accent (how macOS stores the names made in Finder and most apps), and to how a Korean name stores a syllable. Files: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, crates/fffinder-core/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock (one line), docs/manual.md. NEW DIRECT DEPENDENCY of fffinder-core, the owner's call: icu_normalizer 2 with default-features off and `compiled_data`; Cargo.lock had it at 2.4.0 with exactly that feature on Linux, macOS and Windows (through gpui -> url -> idna -> idna_adapter; `cargo tree -i icu_normalizer -e features --target ...` read again in review), so no crate and no feature is added. How it works: `spellings` gives the search as typed, with each such letter as one character, and with each apart; `Engine::search` asks fff-search in each (lowercase and as typed, as for capitals) and merges with `keep_higher`; exclusions are in every search in every spelling; a one-letter search is not repeated. `as_compared` (lowercase + NFC) takes the place of lowercasing wherever a search's words meet a name (`RawHit::rel`, the words, `changes_for`, app names, `rerank`, `name_has`, `name_holds`, quoted phrases). A hit also has its path without accents (`RawHit::bare`, `plain`), where `looked_in` looks for a word typed without any. `letters` + `highlight` light whole letters at positions of the name as stored. `may_be_spelled_apart` is gone. Added in review: `score_scale` (the scores of the searches made in different spellings on one scale), `index_spelling` comparing with `as_compared`, and a run of letters found across an accent that has no character of its own with its letter.
changelog: A name with accented letters is found however it stores them. A name can keep a letter such as `é` as one character or as the letter followed by its accent, which is how macOS stores the names made in Finder and in most apps, and a search typed one way didn't match a name stored the other. `señor` could miss `señor.txt`, or list it only among loose typo matches without a highlight, and never with **Allow typos** off, in a quoted word, or for an app. Both spellings now match and rank alike, with the word highlighted, in words, quoted words and folder filters, and Korean names stored as the parts of their syllables are found the same way. A word typed without accents finds the names that have them, after the names that have the word as typed and among those that have its letters with gaps: `resume` finds `Résumé.pdf`, which it did only for names stored the macOS way. For a name that stores each accent in one character with its letter, that works for up to two accented letters in a word, and in a large folder such a name can be left out when many others match the word loosely. A word typed with an accent is taken as typed, so `résumé` doesn't find `resume.pdf`, and quoted words are compared letter for letter. A misspelled word with an accent or in another alphabet now lists only near misses, as other words do, and what a search opened is remembered for such names too. `fff find` matches the same way.
behaviour_changes: Everything here goes for name searches wherever Engine::search is used: the window, Smart Folders, the file chooser, `fff find`.

A word typed with an accented letter finds names that store the letter either way, and the same typed the other way round (a name copied out of Finder) finds names stored as one character. Before, a name stored the other way was missing whenever another name had the word, and otherwise came only through the typo fallback, without a highlight. The implementer's trunk picture and mine of the same search: `señor` 1 item -> 2.

It holds with Allow typos off, in quoted words, for apps, for folders and Kind: Folder, in folder filters (`/café/ menu` finds the folder stored apart), for exclusions typed with the accent (`menu !café` leaves out both spellings), for one-letter searches (`ï` typed either way lists the same names), and for Korean names stored as the parts of their syllables. All of these are in the commit's tests or in my probe (edges.rs).
Typed whole, apart, or with some letters each way, a search lists the same names in the same order (checked on 60 random trees, 3,106 searches).

Review: names rank alike however they are stored. fff-search scores a match by the characters of the search (about 14 points each), so a name stored apart scored 14 (`señor`), 28 (`résumé`), 42 (a Korean word of three open syllables) or 88 points (four syllables) more than the same name stored as one character, and `한글문서 초안.txt` stored apart was listed ahead of `한글문서.txt` stored whole, last of three. `search_root` now scales each search's scores to those of the search with every letter as one character. After it, a name stored apart scores up to 7 points less than its twin stored whole in my fixtures (0 to 7), so two such names are still not listed newest first between them.

Globs: one typed either way also finds names that store the letter apart. Where letter case is ignored, names storing the letter as one character are still missed unless a `*` is beside the letter, as before (`*café*` and `café*` work; see Found, not fixed).

Highlights are whole letters in the name as stored: a letter is lit with its accent, a Korean syllable whole. A name stored apart had no highlight for a word typed composed, and for a word typed without accents the accents fell outside the lit ranges.

A word typed without accents finds names that have them, counted as real matches (so also with Allow typos off) and ranked after the names with the word as typed, among the names that have its letters with gaps: in my picture `resume` lists resume.pdf, Resume Builder.txt, the three Résumé names stored apart, `restaurant summer menu.txt`, then the two stored whole. For names stored as one character this works while fff-search returns them as typo matches: up to two accented letters in the word, three when the first word has twelve letters or more (`repete` misses `répété.txt` stored whole, `teledeclarer` finds `télédéclarer.txt`; probed), and in a large folder such a name can be cut off (the implementer's 49,638-file tree: `resume` lists the three stored whole 280th to 282nd of 1,345).

Side effects of 'without accents': a one-letter search `e` lists names that have only `é` (after the names with a plain `e`), `cafe` finds `Café.app`, kana without voicing marks find kana with them (`かき` lists `がぎ.txt` last, with 6 points), `istanbul` finds `İstanbul.txt`, `и`/`е` find `й`/`ё`.

A word typed with an accent is taken as typed: `résumé` doesn't find `resume.pdf`, `café menu` doesn't find `cafe menu.txt`, and to Allow typos another accent or none is a wrong letter. A quoted word is letter for letter.

Near misses: an accent no longer counts as a typo against a word typed without any (`bjrok` finds `Björk - Jóga.mp3` stored apart). A misspelled word with an accent or in another alphabet now lists only near misses (the `may_be_spelled_apart` exemption is gone): `bjrök` lists Björk and not `Überblick.md`.
What a search opened is remembered under each spelling, so the opened file ranks first for the search typed either way.
Live results (`changes_for`): a new file whose name stores accents apart counts for a search typed composed, decomposed or without accents.
`fff dirs`: an app stored apart is listed for `café`, `CAFÉ` typed decomposed, and `cafe`. `fff files` and `fff dirs` otherwise still ask fff-search in the spelling typed.

Review: with Follow symbolic links on, a search of one folder whose path was given with an accent spelled another way than the disk has it is searched by the names the index has, as a path in another letter case already was (`index_spelling`; with the setting off it was respelled already). The rule alone is tested: Linux takes the two spellings for two folders.

Cost, debug build. ASCII tree (cargo registry, 49,518 files, nine not ASCII): 424 searches (53 queries, four kinds, Allow typos on and off), each the least of three by processor time, the better of two alternated runs. The implementer's commit against its base: 14.4 s -> 15.2 s (+6%), the 32 one-letter searches among them 2.29 s -> 2.19 s, worst `"Cargo"` 236 -> 274 ms. The trunk commit 362de8f against its parent 4efa254: 15.29 s -> 15.29 s. The implementer's 512 searches by the clock: 14.6 s -> 15.1 s. Lists, 362de8f against 4efa254: 414 of 424 identical in items, order, scores and highlights, the other ten (`mod`, `src/`, `tests/`) differing as much between two runs of one build; the demo folder 424 of 424. Trees with many names beyond ASCII cost more: the implementer's 30,000-file tree, 72% not ASCII, 64 searches 2.8 s -> 9.6 s in this build, where icu_normalizer is not optimized (not measured again). A search typed with an accent is two fff-search searches a location, four with a capital, up to six typed neither way.

Manual: a new paragraph under Search syntax; the Allow typos row loses its sentence about words with an accent or in another alphabet; the folder-filter sentence says other letters must be typed in the letter case the folder has them in.
left_out: `fff files` and `fff dirs` (Engine::list) ask fff-search in the spelling typed alone; only the app names `fff dirs` adds are compared the new way.

A path that stores one accented word each way (two accented words, or a folder filter plus a word) is found only through fff-search's typo matching or not at all: the spellings are per search, not per word.

No ranking bonus for a name found without its accents: it ranks where fff-search puts it, among the paths that have the letters with gaps, as names stored apart did on the trunk. `rerank`, `name_has` (what a sort chooses among) and `spells` go by the letters as typed. Giving such a name a bonus below the as-typed ones would lift `Résumé.pdf` above `restaurant summer menu.txt` for `resume`; it touches the sort's choice too and I left it as a design question.
Accent-blind matching for names stored as one character is as far as fff-search's typo allowance goes (two letters, three from twelve), and its 2,000 best.
Exclusions and folder filters typed without accents are not accent-blind (see Found, not fixed).
The scale is a ratio of character counts; fff-search's fixed bonuses (match at the start of the path, after a separator) are scaled with the rest, which is the few points left between twins.
No release build (forbidden here): no release timing, no binary size. Nothing compiled or run for macOS or Windows. `cargo clippy --features term` not run: no signature that src/term calls changed.
CHANGELOG.md, per the guide. No headless UI test: the behaviour is the engine's, with engine tests, and the window is in the pictures.

review_fixes: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `score_scale` and its use at the end of `search_root`: the merged searches' scores were not on one scale. fff-search scores a match by the characters of the search it found (the unicode path of frizbee: about 12 points a character, 14 with the name bonus), and a search spelled apart has more characters, so a name stored apart outranked the same name stored whole by 14 points an extra character: 88 for a Korean word of four syllables, more than a name that is the word has over one that only has it. In a tree with `한글문서.txt` stored whole and `한글문서 초안.txt` and `새 한글문서.txt` stored apart the exact name came last. Each search's scores are now multiplied by the characters of the composed spelling over the characters of its own, counted in the parts fff-search matched by (`parsed.fuzzy_query`, parts of two bytes or more), so a one-letter search and a search with no words are left alone. The product is made in 64 bits. New test names_rank_alike_however_they_store_their_accents, and assertions on `score_scale` in the pure test.

crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `highlight`: an accent that has no character of its own with its letter (the tilde of `x̃`, Hebrew points, a second accent that doesn't compose) stays an entry by itself in `letters`, after the letter. For a search typed without such accents it stood between its letter and the next, so letters in a row were not seen as a run and the greedy match could light an earlier stray letter instead (`xb` in `xx̃b` lit the first x and the b). Such entries are now left out of the name's letters for a search that has none typed so; the ranges are still whole letters. One assertion; my model of highlight (400,000 rounds) now agrees in every case but a search typed with the accent by itself.

crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `index_spelling` (landed in a085120 while this was in review; its reviewer's note offered this): with Follow symbolic links on, a folder was respelled only for a `..` or a path that differed in letter case alone. The names are now compared with `as_compared`, so a path that differs only in how it spells an accent is respelled too. Two assertions in a_folder_is_searched_by_the_names_its_index_has.

Commit message: the paragraph that said names stored apart come first by 14, 27 and 50 points is replaced by one on the scale; a paragraph on `index_spelling`; the highlight paragraph says what an accent by itself is to a search; my own timing beside the implementer's; the Changelog paragraph says the spellings rank alike.

Rebased from ddefe96 onto ffb02de, 5e68c44, a085120 and 4efa254 (no conflicts). a085120 changed the start of `Engine::search` and `changes_for` (the folder as the index has it); I read both again with this change in place: `spelled`/`respelled` and `may_list` apply as they were, and the engine's 84 tests pass.

Nothing else was changed. I found no fault in `spellings`, `as_compared`, `plain`, `looked_in`, `letters`, the strict check, `changes_for`, `track_open`, the app names or the tests' fixtures (see notes for how they were checked).
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the tree that is the trunk commit 362de8f: 840 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (the same counts on e00b607, which was this commit before the review's highlight fix and the 64-bit product). `git push . HEAD:search-ui-polish` fast-forwarded 4efa254..362de8f. Lane b is clean at the trunk's tip.

NOT pushed to origin. The permission system refused `git push origin search-ui-polish` (auto mode classifier: Destructive or Unwanted Actions), not the network; I did not retry or go around it. `git ls-remote origin search-ui-polish` answers 4efa254. The commit is on the local trunk and the next integration, or the owner, carries it.

How it was checked. (1) The tests against the trunk's behaviour, on the implementer's commit 5778943: the code hunks of the diff reversed (28 hunks outside `mod tests`), the seven helper functions the tests call added back, the commit's tests kept: 7 of the engine's 79 tests fail, for the brief's reasons (`señor` lists only Señor Lopez.txt; changes_for answers nothing; the opened file isn't first; `senor` misses Señor Lopez.txt; case_fit 0; no Café.app; no highlight), 72 pass, among them the pure helper test, whose functions are there. The lane was clean after. Each of my three fixes was shown failing its test without it. (2) A model of `highlight`, `letters`, `as_compared` and `plain` that is told how each letter of a name is spelled and never asks the code (model.rs): 400,000 rounds on the final code, names with capitals, each letter stored whole or apart, searches typed whole, apart or without accents. (3) A model of the search on 60 random trees of 24 names, 3,106 searches with Allow typos on and off: nothing without the word is listed while typos are off; every name that has the word and that fff-search can return for one of the spellings is listed; when a listed name has the word nothing else is listed; the same search typed whole, apart and mixed lists the same names in the same order. 39 names stored whole were not found for a word without accents, which is the limit the manual states. (4) Old against new: 53 ASCII queries in four kinds with typos on and off on the cargo registry and the demo folder, two runs of each build, once for the implementer's commit against its base and once for the trunk commit against its parent (see Cost). (5) fff-search's raw scores per spelling (raw.rs), which is where the review's first fix came from, and the ranked lists in four trees before and after it (rank.rs). (6) Sixty searches of a small tree read one by one (edges.rs): exclusions, folder filters, quoted words, globs, capitals, one letter, kinds, a search of one folder stored apart, sorts, `list`. (7) Six pictures of my own in a copy of the demo folder with names stored both ways, light and dark, looked at: every row's word lit whole, the exact name first, the Korean names in the order exact, begins-with, has. The probes are kept in /home/user/polish-tools/shots/accented-names-search-review2-probes.tar.gz with a README; the implementer's kit is accented-names-search-probe-kit.tar.gz beside it. Wall-clock times here are worthless while the other lanes build (the same binary took 400 to 1,181 ms for one list of searches); I timed by the processor.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what I found. (1) A search that found its item finds nothing, or lists something it shouldn't. For ASCII searches the lists are the trunk's, with scores and highlights. For names with accents the model in (3) found no name lost and none listed without the word; a word typed without accents still finds a name stored apart, which NFC alone would have lost and `RawHit::bare` keeps. What is tighter by intent: a misspelled word with an accent or in another alphabet lists only near misses. (2) The order: names stored one way burying names stored the other. That was real and is the first review fix; what is left is up to 7 points. (3) Every keystroke slower. On an ASCII tree between nothing and +6% processor time in the debug build, one-letter searches no slower. On a tree where most names are beyond ASCII I have no release number: see the first doubt.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. 1. Cost in a release build where most names are not ASCII (a Korean, Japanese or Chinese Mac user's home): every hit's path is respelled (NFC) and looked through for accents at each search of a location, 2,000 to 20,000 hits, and a search typed with such letters is made two to six times. In the debug build that is 3.5 times the trunk's time on the implementer's tree; icu_normalizer is not among the packages the dev profile optimizes (`[profile.dev.package]` in Cargo.toml has fff-search and the UI kit), and adding it there would rebuild much of the tree in every lane, so I left it. By reading icu_normalizer the release cost should be a few lookups a character, well under a microsecond a path, but that is an estimate. 2. macOS was not run. That Finder-made names are stored apart on APFS, that typed text is composed, and that realpath gives a name in the spelling the disk has (which `index_spelling` leans on for letter case too) are from knowledge. The tests compare names composed, so they take either spelling back from the disk; the history test builds its paths from literals, as its neighbours do. 3. The word-without-accents half is partial for names stored as one character and ranks such names among loose matches (left_out). The manual says both. If Finder-like behaviour is wanted there, it needs a name bonus for a match without accents, and a way to get such names out of fff-search past its typo allowance. 4. Folding by canonical decomposition treats kana voicing marks, й and ё, Hebrew and Arabic points and the Indic virama as accents, for words typed without them only; exact names rank first. 5. The dependency. 6. Up to six searches a location for a search typed with a capital and with its accents neither all whole nor all apart; four with a capital and an accent, two with an accent. 7. The scale assumes fff-search's score goes by the characters of the search, which holds for neo_frizbee 0.13.3 (its unicode path, used when the needle isn't ASCII); names_rank_alike_however_they_store_their_accents will say so if a new fff-search scores otherwise.

For briefs still to come.
- near-miss-beside-scattered (lane d, in review at ef165fd on 4efa254): this landed first, so yours rebases over it, and the same lines conflict. `may_be_spelled_apart` is gone and nothing takes its place: names have a word in either spelling now. The check reads `hit.looked_in(w)` where it read `&hit.rel`: the path as compared (lowercase, NFC) for a word that has an accent, the path without accents (`RawHit::bare`) for a word typed without any. Resolve your retain to `let text = hit.looked_in(w); is_subsequence(w, text) || misspelled.contains(&w) && near_miss(w, text, typo_budget(w))`. In `may_be_misspelled` drop the `|| !word.is_ascii()` of the filter (a word of three letters in another alphabet has no typo budget, like any other) and use `hit.looked_in(word)` for both the `contains` and the `is_subsequence`, or a word typed without accents that a name has in a row with accents counts as misspelled. In `near_miss_bonus` the branch for a letter that may be spelled apart goes, and the one before it needs no `word.is_ascii()`: a listed hit that has neither the letters in order nor a near miss in its name has its near miss in a folder's name. Look in `hit.looked_in(word)` there too. The name is `hit.name()` in `rerank` (a Cow of the end of `rel`, already compared), and for a word without accents the name without them is `plain(name)`. `RawHit` has a new field `bare` (tests that build one by hand through `RawHit::file`/`dir` get it; a literal needs `bare: None`). `rerank(hit, &words)` is called in one place. In the manual keep this commit's removal of the Allow typos row's sentence on words with an accent, and its new paragraph under Search syntax. The scores your tests compare are scaled only for searches typed with letters that come apart.
- multi-word-highlights: `highlight(name, needle)` matches over `letters(name)`: the characters of the name as compared, each with the byte range of its whole letter in the name as stored (an accent stored apart, or the parts of a Korean syllable, belong to one letter). `same(c, typed)` lets a letter typed without an accent be the letter with one. Highlight per word over that list and take the ranges from it; never slice a name by positions found in a lowercased or respelled copy. The needle is still every fuzzy word of the search as typed, composed inside `highlight`.
- query-history-boost: `track_open` remembers a search under the text of each spelling (`spellings(&query)`, then the same folding as before), and `search` gives fff-search one text for each. Whatever you add to the text fff-search looks a search up under has to be added for every spelling. `search_root` scales a hit's whole score, the 1,000 points of the opened file included (by 1/3 at the least); a_search_remembers_what_it_opened_however_its_accents_are_stored pins that it stays first.
- fix-folder-search-own-name-pool: `search_root` ends by setting each hit's `rel` (as compared), `bare`, and its scaled score, and is called two to six times a location for a search with letters that come apart; what you change in what is fetched applies to each call. `scale` is taken from `parsed.fuzzy_query` in each of the three branches.
- type-select-space, go-to-folder-keyboard: both compare a typed prefix with names in lowercase (`type_to_select` in src/finder/mod.rs, `tree_type_to_select` in folder_tree.rs, the prefix match in crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs), so a typed `é` never begins a name stored apart. `as_compared` is private to engine.rs; it would have to be made public in the core crate for them. Not in this brief.
- search-settings-hints-steppers: the Allow typos row of the manual no longer says that words with an accent are held to the rule only on paths in A to Z; a hint in the dialog shouldn't either.
- fix-wording-after-later-changes: sentences that are new or changed here: the paragraph beginning "A letter with an accent matches however a name stores it." under Search syntax; in the folder-filter paragraph "other letters, such as `Ü`, must be typed in the letter case the folder has them in"; the Allow typos row, which lost two sentences.
- recent-searches: a recalled search is the text as it was typed; the engine respells it at each search.
- adhoc-index-feedback: `index_spelling` now also respells a folder whose path differs from the disk's only in how an accent is spelled, with Follow symbolic links on.
- content-match-highlight, regex-content-search, search-settings-without-effect, recents-walk-index and the briefs that only touch src/finder: independent. Contents searches are not touched: they still compare text as it is stored.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- A glob with a letter beyond ASCII that has a capital finds nothing where letter case is ignored unless a `*` is beside the letter: `fold_case` makes `[éÉ]`, and fff-search's globs match a set byte by byte (the implementer's finding; `*москва*` finds nothing on the trunk either). `*café*` and `café*` work, in both spellings.
- A Greek name in capitals whose last sigma is before the extension, `ΣΙΣΥΦΟΣ.txt`, is not found by the word as it is written in lowercase, `σισυφος`, with Allow typos off, and only as a near miss without a highlight with it on (probed): `to_lowercase` makes that sigma `σ` because `.txt` follows it, and the typed word ends in `ς`. Typed `σισυφοσ` it is found and lit. Folding `ς` to `σ` in `as_compared` and in `letters` would cure it.
- An exclusion typed without accents (`menu !cafe`) leaves out a name that stores the accent apart, whose bytes have `cafe`, and not a name that stores it as one character (probed: Café Bar/menu.txt stays, Café/menu.txt stored apart goes). Typed with the accent it leaves out both. fff-search matches an exclusion by the bytes.
- A folder filter typed without the accent (`/munchen/ karte`) finds nothing; `/münchen/ karte` does, in either spelling. The manual's folder-filter paragraph says other letters must be typed.
- `strasse` doesn't find `straße.txt`: `ß` has no decomposition and lowercasing keeps it.
- `SearchResponse::total_matched` counts what fff-search matched for the first spelling of a search only. Nothing reads it outside the engine's tests.
- Type to select in the views and the folder tree, and Go to Folder's suggestions, compare prefixes in lowercase, so a typed `é` never begins a name stored apart (see the notes for those briefs).
- With a list that is not full and no `+`, matches can still be missing because fff-search's best 2,000 are cut before the engine's check; result-tie-break's record has this.
